method.design: Same matched-pair design as the Booking.com diff. Treatment = client's authenticated Chrome. Control = inspector instance, signed out, extension-clean, consent declined.

result.verification: Signed-out page text searched for 'track prices' and for any 'track' language — zero matches. Not inferred from a missing control; confirmed against full page text.

finding_F28.claim: Authentication unlocks exactly one capability on Google Travel, and it is a functional one — persistent price monitoring — not a discount.

finding_F29_THE_CONTRAST.claim: Two products, two matched-pair diffs, one extra capability each — but of opposite kinds.

evidence.Booking.com: Signing in adds ONE sort axis: 'Genius discounts first'. A commercial unlock — another way to rank by price.
evidence.Google Travel: Signing in adds ONE capability: 'Track prices'. A functional unlock — the product does something over time that it otherwise cannot.

finding_F29_THE_CONTRAST.why_it_matters_for_luma: Both products ask a traveller to create an account. Booking.com's answer to 'why should I?' is a better price; Google's is a capability that persists between sessions. For a first-time traveller — who has no booking history to convert into a discount — only the second kind of reason is available on day one. This is a directly usable answer to the retention problem F-18 left open.
finding_F29_THE_CONTRAST.scope_limit: Two products. Expedia's logged-out state was not captured, so its diff is OWED and its absence is a real gap in this comparison.

our_product_decision_required: Decision required: what does a Luma account BUY on day one, before any booking exists? Booking.com's and Expedia's answers both require history the target user does not have. Google's does not.

Decision required: price tracking is monitoring over time — it implies the product acts while the traveller is away. That is the same shape as Luma's stated 'live flight tracking' and 'gate notifications'. Is watching-on-your-behalf the account's core value rather than a discount?
owed: Expedia logged-out control capture — its matched pair is missing and F-29 currently rests on two of three
